explanation: For each transaction count, keep the least effective buying price after accounting for previous profits, and the greatest completed profit. Update counts downward: sell at the current price or lower the effective buy price. If k cannot bind, sum positive adjacent gains.
timeComplexity: O(n·min(k,n)); O(n) when k≥n/2 The limited case visits n prices and k transaction states; the unlimited case makes one pass.
spaceComplexity: O(k) state in the limited-transactions branch; O(n) temporary storage in the unlimited branch because prices[:-1] and prices[1:] create slices.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/buy_and_sell_stock_k_times.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: min_prices[i] is the least cost of holding a share for transaction i+1 after earlier profits, and max_profits[i] is the best profit after at most i+1 sales. Selling gains price−min_prices[i]; buying costs price−max_profits[i−1]. Descending updates preserve the prior-day dependency. When 2k≥n, every rising segment can be traded, and the sum of positive adjacent gains is optimal.
walkthrough: For prices [5,1,4,2,7] and k=2, buy at 1 and sell at 4 for 3, then buy at 2 and sell at 7 for 5. The combined best profit is 8.
edgeCases: A large k reduces to taking every positive adjacent gain.
At most one share may be held at any time.
